incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: sustained preproc CPU >95% on deployment token-preproc-prod-usw2. Multiple pods OOMKilled, 502/500 errors rising to ~18% over last 5m. Auto-scaling not keeping up. Paging @mia (oncall) and @sam (sre). Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/token-preproc-oom

mia (oncall): Oncall ack — I'm looking. Any signal on whether this is tokenization hotloop or a larger input flood?

sam (sre): seeing massive short prompts with big regex in parse stage, spikes correlate with a single customer IP range. Kernel OOM logs show process killed due to RSS growth then SIGKILL.

jordan (infra): grabbing logs from one of the OOM pods now. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T21:01:09Z] preproc[pid=2345] CRIT: OutOfMemoryError: RSS 1.9GiB > limit 1.8GiB
[2026-03-15T21:01:09Z] kernel: mycontainer invoked oom-killer: gfp_mask=0x2
[2026-03-15T21:01:09Z] preproc[pid=2345] TRACE: tokenization loop: input_len=42000, regex_count=22
```

lee (eng-runtime): quick mitigation idea: enable token-throttle config to drop/trim extremely long prompts and circuit-break the preproc path. We can also patch deployment to reduce cpu limits to favor eviction over host OOMs.

sam (sre): Agree. Steps I propose, in order:
1) Patch token-preproc ConfigMap to enable token_throttle: true + max_tokens=8192
2) Scale preproc replicas from 8 -> 16 for short term
3) Route traffic for flagged customer IP range to fallback
